title: 6 Rules for Calendar UX Design
summary: This lesson outlines a systematic approach to calendar UI, focusing on layout rules that improve readability and interaction. It covers grid structure, color usage, event overlapping, and drag-and-drop behaviors.

transcript.text: A week, forty events, zero overlap, six layout rules.
Seven columns, 24 rows, one hour each.
Hour labels sit on the line, not in the cell.
A red line marks now.
The view opens scrolled to it, not to midnight.
Color per calendar. A three-pixel stripe on the left.
The fill at 10%.
The title stays readable on every color.
Full fills turn a busy week into a rainbow.
Two events, same hour, side by side, half width each.
Three, a third.
Never stacked, never hidden behind a plus one.
Height is duration. One hour, 60 pixels.
15 minutes still gets a title on a single line, clipped.
Under that, a bar you can hover.
Drag on empty space, an event draws.
Snap to 15 minutes.
Move by the body, resize by the bottom edge only.
The time label updates while you drag, not after.
All day events live in a pinned row above the grid.
They never eat the morning.
Scroll the hours, the row stays.
Six rules, one week that reads at a glance.
Now make Claude Code think like a senior UX designer.
UX Engine designs the screen before coding, audits what is broken, reviews the diff, and kills the AI look.
Link in bio.

All day lives in a pinned row.
Six rules. One week that reads.
Think like a senior UX designer.
design_principles: Grid alignment: Labels on lines for better scanning.
Contextual defaults: Scroll to current time instead of midnight.
Visual clarity: Use 10% fills and 3px stripes to avoid 'rainbow' visual noise.
Information density: Side-by-side events instead of hiding data behind '+1' buttons.
Immediate feedback: Update labels during drag interactions, not after.
Layout persistence: Pin all-day events so they don't consume grid space.
before_after: Contrasts 'Full Fills' (busy/rainbow look) with 'Stripes' (clean/readable look), and 'Hidden behind +1' with 'Side-by-side' visibility.
